'''Bruno Coppi''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|OMRI]]}} (born 19 November 1935 in [[Gonzaga, Lombardy]], [[Italy]]) is an Italian-American physicist specializing in [[plasma physics]].

In 1959, Coppi attained an Italian doctoral degree at [[Polytechnic University of Milan]] and was subsequently a docent and research scientist at the Polytechnic Institute and the [[University of Milan]]. In 1961, he was a scientist at the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]]. From 1964 to 1967, he was an assistant professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]], from 1967 to 1969 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and from 1968 a professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. In the 1980s, Coppi was a member of the science team in the [[Voyager 2]] space probe.

Coppi works on theoretical plasma physics, space plasmas and magnetic fusion. At MIT, he initiated the [[Alcator C-Mod|Alcator Program]], which led to the Russian-Italian [[IGNITOR|Ignitor proposal]], which aimed at building a high-field breakeven tokamak near Moscow, with Coppi as the principal investigator.<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2010/fusion-ignition-0510.html MIT News 2010 on the Ignitor Program]</ref> In addition, Coppi has taken a leading role in the [[Frascati Tokamak Upgrade|Frascati Torus Program]] in Italy.

In 2018, MIT spun out the private company [[Commonwealth Fusion Systems]], aiming to operate a high field breakeven [[tokamak]]. MIT described it as an evolution of concepts initiated by Bruno Coppi and Ron Parker.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.mit.edu/2018/mit-newly-formed-company-launch-novel-approach-fusion-power-0309|title=MIT and newly formed company launch novel approach to fusion power|date=9 March 2018|first=David|last=Chandler|publisher=MIT News Office|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180310064636/https://news.mit.edu/2018/mit-newly-formed-company-launch-novel-approach-fusion-power-0309|archive-date=10 March 2018}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1987, Coppi received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Coppi&first_nm=Bruno&year=1987|title=1987 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516052948/http://www.aps.org:80/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Coppi&first_nm=Bruno&year=1987 |archive-date=2011-05-16 |access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> and also the Award of Excellence in Plasma Physics from the [[American Physical Society]]. He is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (since 1976), the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[Accademia Nazionale Virgiliana di Scienze Lettere ed Arti|National Virgilian Academy of Sciences, Letters and Arts]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of academicians of the National Virgilian Academy |url=https://www.accademianazionalevirgiliana.org/ANV21/index.php/corpo |access-date=2022-06-11 |archive-date=2022-05-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524024011/https://www.accademianazionalevirgiliana.org/ANV21/index.php/corpo |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. He received the American Dante Alighieri Prize, the Science Prize of the Italian government, the science and technology prize from Italgas, and the gold medal of the Milan Polytechnic Institute.{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}}

In 2000, he was knighted Grand Officer of the [[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quirinale.it/onorificenze/insigniti/72359|title=Le onorificenze della Repubblica Italiana|website=www.quirinale.it|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref>

In 2016, Coppi won the [[Feltrinelli Prize|Antonio Feltrinelli International Prize for Chemistry and Physics]] from the [[Accademia nazionale dei Lincei]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/news/bourgain-feltrinelliprize|title=Jean Bourgain Wins 2016 Antonio Feltrinelli International Prize|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=10 June 2016 |language=en|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref>
